slides.texte_overlay:
Habits that make you
sound smarter instantly
Use numbers when you can. Not "a lot of people" but "about a third of them." Specific numbers sound thoughtful, even in casual conversation, and people trust them more.
Say "I'm not sure, but I think" instead of guessing loudly. Smart people show their confidence level. Pretending to be certain about everything is exactly what makes people sound clueless.
Give one example for every big claim. "Small habits matter. Like how making your bed starts the day with a win." Examples make ideas stick, and they make you sound like you really get it.
Ask good follow-up questions. "What made you decide that?" or "What surprised you most?" Curious questions sound smarter than clever statements, and they make people love talking to you.
Slow down by ten percent. Fast talkers sound nervous. A slightly slower pace with clear pauses makes even simple ideas sound considered. It's the easiest change you can make today.
Summarise before you add. "So if I get it right, you're saying..." It shows you listened, and it makes whatever you say next sound sharper and more relevant to the conversation.
Read and learn a little every day. Five minutes of history, art or science gives you references and words most people don't have. Smart-sounding people are just well-fed minds.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: nothing to add when the talk got deep. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I've always got a reference ready.
